newsitem.title: CHINA: Cold China weather said not to affect grain output.
newsitem.headline: Cold China weather said not to affect grain output.

text.p: Recent cold weather is unlikely to affect China's grain production and a bumper harvest is expected for 1997, the China Daily said on Friday.
A cold snap over the last week may freeze wheat in areas south of the Yangtze river but should benefit wheat in northern China, it quoted Zhao Hanjie, a Ministry of Agriculture official, as saying.
In the dry north, the cold kills pests and disease, supplies moisture and cleans the air, he said.

In the south, the success of wheat sown later than usual last year because of rains would depend on the spring weather, he said. Normal spring growth should bring another bumper harvest in the summer, which accounts for one-quarter of total grain output.
China estimates its 1996 harvest at a record 480 million tonnes, up from a previous record of 466 million last year.
However, officials warned that a slide in market prices for some cereals could dampen the incentives to farmers to plant grain and affect output.

Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said on Thursday that the government had raised the price the state pays to farmers for grain by 50 percent in 1996 compared with 1995 and domestic grain prices were now higher than both imported grain prices and production costs.
Zhu said the market price for wheat and rice was higher than state purchasing prices and only the price of corn was lower than the market price because of a large harvest.
